original_value: Multifractal denoising techniques capture interest in biomedicine, economy, and signal and image processing. Regarding stroke data there are subtle details not easily detectable by eye physicians. For the stroke subtypes diagnosis, details are important due to including hidden information concerning the possible existence of medical history, laboratory results, and treatment details. Recently, K‐means and fuzzy C means (FCM) algorithms have been applied in literature with many datasets. We present efficient clustering algorithms to eliminate irregularities for a given set of stroke dataset using 2D multifractal denoising techniques (Bayesian (mBd), Nonlinear (mNold), and Pumping (mPumpD)). Contrary to previous methods, our method embraces the following assets: (a) not applying the reduction of the stroke datasets’ attributes, leading to an efficient clustering comparison of stroke subtypes with the resulting attributes; (b) detecting attributes that eliminate “insignificant” irregularities while keeping “meaningful” singularities; (c) yielding successful clustering accuracy performance for enhancing stroke data qualities. Therefore, our study is a comprehensive comparative study with stroke datasets obtained from 2D multifractal denoised techniques applied for K‐means and FCM clustering algorithms. Having been done for the first time in literature, 2D mBd technique, as revealed by results, is the most successful feature descriptor in each stroke subtype dataset regarding the mentioned algorithms’ accuracy rates.

result.paraphrase: Multifractal denoising methods are of interest in biomedicine, economics, and signal and image processing. In stroke data, there are subtle details that are not easily seen by physicians. For diagnosing stroke subtypes, such details matter because they may contain hidden information about possible medical history, laboratory findings, and treatment details. Recently, K-means and fuzzy C means (FCM) algorithms have been used in the literature across many datasets. We introduce efficient clustering algorithms to remove irregularities from a given stroke dataset using 2D multifractal denoising techniques: Bayesian (mBd), Nonlinear (mNold), and Pumping (mPumpD). Unlike prior approaches, our method has the following advantages: (a) it does not reduce the stroke datasets’ attributes, enabling an efficient clustering comparison of stroke subtypes using the resulting attributes; (b) it identifies attributes that remove “insignificant” irregularities while preserving “meaningful” singularities; and (c) it achieves strong clustering accuracy for improving stroke data quality. Therefore, our study is a comprehensive comparative analysis of stroke datasets obtained from 2D multifractal denoised techniques applied to K-means and FCM clustering algorithms. Done for the first time in the literature, the 2D mBd technique, according to the results, is the most successful feature descriptor in each stroke subtype dataset in terms of the accuracy rates of the mentioned algorithms.
